All work is done and verified. Summary:

**Fix applied to `/home/user/Jarvis/systems/dream-cycle/salience-score.py`:**
1. `update_salience_block()` — the removal regex's trailing repetition group changed from `(?:[ \t]+[^\n]*\n)*` to `(?:[ \t]+[^\n]*\n?)*` so the salience block's last line (never newline-terminated because `fm_section = content[3:end]` excludes the newline before the closing `---`) is consumed by the strip instead of stranded.
2. `parse_frontmatter()` — `promoted_m` changed from `re.search()` (first match) to `list(re.finditer(...))[-1]` (last match), so a stray earlier orphan line can never shadow the authoritative current value.

**Verification (acceptance test from the entry):**
- Ran the patched scorer against the full 296-file `memory/episodic` corpus — `yaml.safe_load()` parses all 296 files' frontmatter cleanly, 0 failures, exactly one `salience:` block per file.
- Ran the scorer a second consecutive time on the same date and diffed byte-for-byte against the first run: identical, 0 new orphan lines — directly disproving the "fires on every write" behavior documented in J571BH and 284VH8.
